as_told.title: Larry O'Brien as Howard Hughes lobbyist and the motive for the Watergate break-in

plain: In 1972 burglars broke into the Democratic Party's national offices at the Watergate building in Washington, and the lawyer Dan Sheehan says they were there to bug Larry O'Brien, the party chairman, because O'Brien had earlier been the main Washington lobbyist for the billionaire Howard Hughes. According to Sheehan, President Richard Nixon was terrified of this and wanted to learn whether O'Brien knew about a secret Hughes operation and might use it, so he ordered the phone tapped and the office bugged. Sheehan tells this on two episodes without naming a source, and Michels repeats it twice, adding that the burglar James McCord, a former CIA security man, "wasn't clued in" on why, and once describing O'Brien as running George McGovern's campaign.
